stories.title: Desk workers report rise in AI-generated workslop
stories.summary: A 2025 survey by BetterUp Labs and the Stanford Social Media Lab found 40 percent of US desk workers received AI-generated work that looked polished but failed to move tasks forward. The phenomenon is described as workslop. Machines are producing more than we can read.

stories.title: Defining the user journey map
stories.summary: A journey map visualizes the process a person follows to accomplish a goal. It begins by compiling user actions into a timeline, then incorporates thoughts and emotions to create a narrative. This narrative is eventually condensed and refined into the final map.

stories.title: Software development adapts to AI speed
stories.summary: As AI agents write more code, software development is shifting toward a model similar to digital photography. Because each iteration costs almost nothing, developers can take dozens of frames, adjust, and shoot again. Learning now happens after the shot rather than during the setup.

stories.title: Ubisoft shifts feedback process for Rainbow Six Siege
stories.summary: Following the 2025 #SaveSiege movement, Ubisoft moved from collecting feedback after development to involving players directly during the process. The company says the system was established to rebuild player trust. The results were shared during a media presentation in Osaka.

stories.title: View Royal updates municipal website
stories.summary: View Royal has updated its municipal website to improve accessibility and navigation. The town says the refreshed design creates a more modern, user-friendly experience. Updates include larger text, clickable areas, and a responsive layout that adapts to different screen sizes.

stories.title: Atkinson Hyperlegible typeface expanded
stories.summary: Graphic designer Megan Eiswerth helped develop the Atkinson Hyperlegible typeface for the Braille Institute of America. The font family, which was expanded in 2025, is free to use. The original design was added to the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum permanent collection in 2024.

stories.title: Walmart customer service AI leads to account cancellation
stories.summary: A New York Times writer cancelled her Walmart account after spending over an hour attempting to reach a human through the retailer's AI customer service tool. The company is currently the second-biggest in the world by revenue. The solution to the frustration was total departure.

stories.title: Core77 weekly design roundup
stories.summary: The latest Core77 roundup highlights various industrial and UX design firms. Featured studios include Bould Design, Studio RedEye, Acorn Product Development, ANDESIGN, and Tactile. The publication continues to track strategic partners and independent agencies helping brands drive change across physical and digital products.

stories.title: AI acts as new gatekeeper for consumer choices
stories.summary: Morgan Stanley estimates that agent-influenced shopping could account for a significant portion of future retail. AI now influences brand consideration before shoppers visit a website or open a chatbot. Mental availability is no longer formed directly by traditional communications and shopper experience.

stories.title: BOND creates brand identity for Aleph Farms
stories.summary: BOND designed the brand identity for Aleph Farms by flipping the ancient aleph character to resemble an ox. The studio describes the project as turning steak on its head. The company grows meat from animal cells without raising or slaughtering animals.

stories.title: Studio Freight reimagines Thesis brand identity
stories.summary: Studio Freight built the Thesis brand identity using zine culture aesthetics, including dot-grid type and electric lime accents. The system centers on an asterisk mark. The studio says the identity is intended to read like a samizdat pamphlet that learned to behave on a screen.

stories.title: Material honesty in recent design releases
stories.summary: Recent studio releases emphasize material honesty, from one-side-waxed kraft butter wrappers to translucent vellum soap pouches. Design firms including Pentagram, Studio Hi Ho, and eTypes are utilizing paper and ink as working tools. The trend highlights physical textures in modern packaging.

stories.title: Hey Studio uses real ribbon for Julia wordmark
stories.summary: Hey Studio created the wordmark for Julia coffee shop by photographing real ribbon. The identity keeps the folds, creases, and shadows of the hand-formed letters. The design was built around the act of tying a bow to represent taking extra time.

stories.title: Underline Studio redesigns Toronto Symphony Orchestra identity
stories.summary: Underline Studio reimagined the Toronto Symphony Orchestra identity with an animated S that responds to music. The monogram features T and O characters alongside an S that splits into crescents. The ensemble sought a closer connection with audiences during live performances.

stories.title: Gretel updates Philadelphia Museum of Art identity
stories.summary: Gretel rebuilt the Philadelphia Museum of Art identity using a revived griffin and custom serif type. The museum reintroduced itself with a shortened name in 2025 before restoring its full name in 2026. The griffin design was sourced from existing cornices on the building.

stories.title: The Collected Works designs Circuit civic brand
stories.summary: The Collected Works developed a unified brand identity for the electric shuttle service Circuit. The project aims to consolidate the patchwork look of fifty different city pilot programs into a single operator identity. The design includes transit arrows and standardized fleet wraps.

stories.title: Koto refreshes Nubank brand identity
stories.summary: Koto updated the Nubank brand identity to create a flexible system for its 140 million customers. The refresh includes the introduction of proprietary typefaces, Nu Sans Display and Nu Sans Text. The system uses modular layers to scale across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia.

stories.title: Unfolded designs typography-only book cover
stories.summary: Studio unfolded designed the cover for NZZ Libro's Die neue Polis using only typography. A nineteen-line block of bold italic serif copy sits on the front board, replacing traditional photography or illustrations. The design places political blurbs on the exterior of the book.

stories.title: Adobe Max 2026 shifts focus to on-device AI
stories.summary: Adobe Max 2026 announcements largely centered on cloud-based Firefly and model library updates. Despite this, company leadership noted a strategic shift toward on-device capabilities. The cloud remains the opening act for the company's current AI roadmap.

stories.title: Adobe adds agentic layer to Creative Cloud
stories.summary: Adobe has introduced workflow planning and always-on agents to its Creative Cloud suite. The company claims it is targeting professional creatives with these tools. Management maintains a creative-first approach to differentiate its offerings from free alternatives.

stories.title: Adobe introduces creative agents and governance tools
stories.summary: Adobe has launched Creative Agent assistants and local integrations allowing third-party agents to edit native files. The company has not yet specified which rules take precedence when brand guidelines conflict. Marketing teams are advised to map every agent route before the private beta opens in 2027.

stories.title: Adobe previews experimental creative tools at MAX Sneaks
stories.summary: Adobe showcased ten research projects at its MAX Sneaks event, including tools for relighting images and brush-based AI. These previews are not finished features, though Adobe notes that previous Sneaks projects have historically influenced software updates. The company aims to reduce manual creative tasks.

stories.title: Adobe updates Firefly and GenStudio with AI agents
stories.summary: Adobe announced a wave of AI-powered upgrades across its Creative Cloud and GenStudio platforms at MAX 2026. The company intends to automate repetitive creative tasks and strengthen partnerships with Google and Microsoft. Adobe aims to become the primary toolbox for automated creative workflows.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Design for prototyping
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Design, a tool powered by its Opus 4.7 vision model. The product is designed to allow users to create prototypes and presentations without traditional graphic software. The company describes the AI as a brush that turns ideas into visual reality.

stories.title: Designers shift workflows toward AI-integrated tools
stories.summary: The PUSH UX conference highlighted a divide between teams experimenting with AI and those integrating it into daily processes. One designer reported moving 90 percent of his work from Figma to Claude Code. The event emphasized that process changes are more significant than tool changes.

stories.title: Google Labs updates Stitch interface design tool
stories.summary: Google Labs has expanded its Stitch tool to support multiple artboards and additional file types. The interface uses Gemini 2.5 Pro to convert text and sketches into frontend code. The tool now includes a draft specification file for design standards.

stories.title: Figma and Stanford release animation benchmark
stories.summary: Researchers from Figma and Stanford University have introduced MotionGraphicsBench to evaluate how large language models animate static vector graphics. The benchmark uses programmatic verification to assess 100 tasks. It aims to provide a reproducible alternative to subjective human scoring.

stories.title: Figma Earnings Call: AI Adoption Lifts Growth and Outlook - TipRanks
Substack adds website design controls
stories.summary: Substack has launched seven new website themes and additional layout controls for publishers. The updated editor allows users to customize typography and colors while previewing changes across different screens. A shuffle button provides random combinations for those seeking new layouts.

stories.title: Canva launches Craft image generation model
stories.summary: Canva has introduced its Craft AI image model to compete with existing generators. The company claims its research lab is the second most advanced in the world for image generation. Reviewers noted similar performance between Canva and ChatGPT in recent product photography tests.

stories.title: Canva enters AI image generation market
stories.summary: Canva has launched its first in-house AI image model, Canva Craft. The tool is designed to integrate image generation with the company's existing design platform for social media and marketing materials. Canva suggests the tool provides a unified workflow for its users.

stories.title: Adobe showcases experimental AI research
stories.summary: Adobe demonstrated several experimental technologies at its MAX Sneaks event, including tools for automated creative work. The company uses the showcase to share research that may influence future software features. Adobe researchers continue to explore ways to automate tasks currently performed by hand.

stories.title: Canva research head outlines AI strategy
stories.summary: Canva's head of AI research, Stefano Corazza, stated that the company's Craft model plans designs before rendering. Corazza argues that Canva's advantage lies in its access to interaction data from 250 million monthly users. He describes AI as an iterative companion rather than a replacement.

stories.title: Canva leverages user data for AI model development
stories.summary: Canva is utilizing behavior signals from its 250 million monthly users to train its Craft image model. Research lead Stefano Corazza stated that owning the editing surface provides a competitive edge over frontier AI labs. The company claims this data informs its design planning process.

stories.title: AgentGrid launches visual collaboration canvas
stories.summary: AgentGrid has introduced a visual interface called Canvas. The tool is designed to facilitate collaboration with AI agents. It provides a workspace for users to interact with agentic workflows.

stories.title: Adobe expands Firefly with design and workflow tools
stories.summary: Adobe has released beta versions of Firefly Design and Firefly Graph. The tools provide a shared canvas for creative work and allow users to build repeatable workflows. A private beta for third-party agent connections is scheduled for early 2027.

stories.title: AD Design Show 2026 explores apartment evolution
stories.summary: At the AD Design Show in Mumbai, architects discussed the unbuilding of apartments, using red ant patterns to argue that living spaces should not be static. Another session explored reclaiming ground by moving beyond a mono-culture of time. The ocean was not mentioned, but the apartment was.

stories.title: Coimbatore home sheds its lifeless past
stories.summary: A family of five in Coimbatore has renovated their two-storey home after living for nearly a decade with ready-made furniture and fluorescent lighting. The homeowner described the previous space as completely lifeless. The family has now moved on to more vibrant colours and textures.

stories.title: PNG Jewellers rebrands its lightweightdiamond jewellery brand Litestyle as ‘YOOU’ - The Retail Jeweller India
Design to play key role in India’s decisive decade of development: Piyush Goyal - DD News
Graphon Labs secures $35 million for AI memory
stories.summary: Graphon Labs has raised $35 million in a Series A round to build a persistent-memory platform for AI agents. The company aims to maintain relationships among data sources as reusable infrastructure rather than reconstructing them. The funding brings the total raised to $43.3 million.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath calls bulldozers a brand identity for UP
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has encouraged increased manufacturing of bulldozers, calling them a brand identity for the state. Speaking at a new facility opening, he claimed that a zero tolerance policy toward crime has improved law and order. The bulldozers remain in production.

stories.title: Privacyboard
NID Jorhat seeks visiting medical officer
stories.summary: The National Institute of Design in Jorhat has invited applications for a single visiting medical officer position on a contract basis. Candidates must hold an MBBS degree and possess at least three years of experience in a recognized hospital. The institute is currently accepting applications.

stories.title: Porto Rocha designs new identity for Almeida & Dale
stories.summary: Porto Rocha has unveiled a new brand identity for the gallery Almeida & Dale, featuring a custom typeface and a single strong blue. The design system applies the colour across all materials. The gallery became Latin America's largest following a 2025 merger, but the work remains quiet.

stories.title: StitchStudio raises $8 million for insurance automation
stories.summary: StitchStudio has raised $8 million in a funding round led by Voyager Capital to expand its AI platform for insurance operations. The company plans to use the capital for product development and self-service capabilities. Customers claim the software reduces the time required for producer contracting.

stories.title: Graphon Raises $35M for Persistent AI Agent Memory
stories.summary: Graphon Raises $35M to Give AI Agents Memory Beyond the Context Window San Francisco-based Graphon Labs raised a $35 million Series A led by RRE Ventures on November 10, 2026, bringing its total funding to $43.3 million less than six months after an $8.3 million seed round. stories.title: C2i Semiconductors raises $15 million
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based C2i Semiconductors has raised $15 million in a Series A round led by Peak XV Partners. The funding is the largest secured by an Indian semiconductor startup to date. The sector is traditionally considered high-risk due to heavy R&D investment and long development cycles.

stories.title: Tendrils Compute raises $30 million for interaction net chips
stories.summary: Cambridge-based Tendrils Compute has raised $30 million to develop general-purpose chips based on interaction nets. The startup is challenging conventional CPU and GPU designs but has not yet released hardware benchmarks. Investors are backing the company alongside two other UK chip firms.

stories.title: Indian startup funding drops to 2026 low
stories.summary: Venture capital funding into Indian startups fell to $26 million across 11 deals during the second week of November. This marks the lowest weekly level for 2026, a sharp decline from the $263 million recorded the previous week. The festive period was cited as a contributing factor.

stories.title: Startup funding activity slows in India
stories.summary: Indian startups raised $25.2 million across nine deals between November 9 and November 13, a 90.1 percent decline from the previous week. The number of deals also fell by 55 percent. The post-festive period has seen a significant pullback in capital inflows.

stories.title: LangChain valuation reaches $3 billion
stories.summary: Agent management startup LangChain has raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation, led by CapitalG. The company, which began as an open source project, now focuses on managing AI agents. Its valuation has more than doubled since its previous funding round a year ago.

stories.title: Brothers International updates brand identity
stories.summary: Brothers International has unveiled a new brand identity to reflect its growth as an ingredient platform. The update follows 25 years of operations, including strategic acquisitions and investments in its global supply network. The company says the change represents its evolution into an end-to-end provider.

stories.title: What Is A Business Designer? Business Design In 2026 - FourWeekMBA
Fashion design versus fashion communication
stories.summary: NIFT 2027 students are weighing the differences between fashion design and fashion communication. Fashion design focuses on creating garments, silhouettes, and fabrics. Fashion communication involves branding, styling, and digital content to tell a story. Both paths exist within the fashion world, though the daily tasks differ.

stories.title: Creative Work is Teamwork: SNHU's First Graphic Storytelling Challenge - Southern New Hampshire University
University of the Ozarks adds graphic design major
stories.summary: University of the Ozarks senior Jadaan Anderson declared a graphic design major shortly after the program launched last year. The marketing and graphic design student recently completed a summer placement with Dover Digital. The university is now providing students with opportunities to gain professional experience.

stories.title: For Stefan Sagmeister, short-term everything is crap, long-term everything is fantastic - adobo Magazine
Lalit Kala Akademi hosts 65th national exhibition
stories.summary: The Lalit Kala Akademi in New Delhi recently held its 65th National Exhibition of Art, awarding 20 artists for their work. The event is part of a series showcasing aesthetics and technique. YourStory has documented over 1,000 similar events since 2014 to celebrate creativity and innovation.

stories.title: Chennai arts festival concludes third edition
stories.summary: The Contemporary Now arts festival recently finished its third edition across 10 venues in Chennai. The event aims to highlight opportunities within the art ecosystem beyond the creation of individual works. YourStory continues to document these festivals as part of its long-running weekly photo series.

stories.title: Lessons on self-belief from Be Delusional
stories.summary: In Be Delusional, author Harinder Singh Pelia argues that success requires believing in one's potential before evidence exists. The book encourages readers to pursue ambitious goals without waiting for external approval or ideal circumstances. It suggests that strong self-belief is the primary driver of extraordinary achievement.

stories.title: Yoshuku and the practice of pre-celebration
stories.summary: Azumi Uchitani introduces the Japanese concept of Yoshuku in her book on manifesting. The practice involves expressing gratitude and celebrating a desired future as though it has already happened. The author claims this approach changes how individuals approach their goals by celebrating before success actually arrives.
